findings.title: ShinyHunters Claims 335M Binance User Records Stolen, Demands $900k
findings.summary_md: ThreatMon reported that a threat actor using the ShinyHunters handle posted a listing on an underground forum claiming to have stolen 335 million verified Binance user records. The post allegedly includes sensitive data such as private wallet keys, internal infrastructure details, and user KYC documents, and demands $900,000 with a threat to leak the data otherwise.

findings.title: Binance calls ShinyHunters' alleged 335 million user data breach a likely scam
findings.summary_md: Finwire reported that Binance called the ShinyHunters claim of stealing 335 million user records a likely scam, with no evidence of compromised systems or customer data. ThreatMon said the listing offered 335,900,000 lines of information tied to Binance users across roughly 170 countries for $900,000 in Bitcoin or Monero. Brandefense documented similar advertisements dating back to October without confirming the data was genuine.

findings.title: Binance data breach claim over 335.9 million lines is likely a scam, exchange says
findings.summary_md: The Cryptonomist reported Binance disputing a claim advertising 335.9 million lines of user information, saying its initial review pointed to a likely scam. Binance's customer-support account published that assessment on November 8, 2026, while Brandefense said on November 3 it had examined four versions of related Telegram advertisements without opening a sample. The article noted a separate October 29, 2026 wallet attack affecting about $6.34 billion in digital assets was unrelated.

findings.title: Binance Says 335.9 Million-record Breach Claim Is Likely A Scam
findings.summary_md: Dataconomy reported Binance saying a forum listing claiming 335.9 million lines of user data is likely a scam while it continues investigating. Brandefense's research team said on November 3 it had reviewed four versions of related Telegram advertisements but had not opened or tested any sample. ThreatMon reported the seller sought $900,000 payable in Bitcoin or Monero and put a sample behind a forum paywall.
